issues.description: Script uses GM_xmlhttpRequest to send requests to api.torn.com. The API key is stored in localStorage and can be set by the user. No evidence of sending page content, cookies, or sensitive user data beyond the API key.
issues.location: GM_xmlhttpRequest usage and API key handling
issues.recommendation: Ensure API key is not reused elsewhere and only minimal required data is sent. Consider encrypting API key in storage if possible.

issues.description: Script reads and writes API key to localStorage. No evidence of reading cookies, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or clipboard. No keylogger or form data extraction.
issues.recommendation: Ensure API key is not sensitive or reused for other purposes. Warn users not to use private keys.

issues.description: Script uses setTimeout with a function, not a string. No eval, new Function, or dynamic script loading. No @require in metadata.
No evidence of code obfuscation, base64 decoding, unicode encoding, or minified code.
No evidence of DOM XSS or injection. User input (API key) is only used for API requests and not inserted into DOM.
Script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest, GM_addStyle, GM_registerMenuCommand. All are used in code. No unused high privilege grants.
No sensitive API calls (geolocation, RTCPeerConnection, MediaDevices, clipboard, notifications).
No @require or third-party library loading. No supply chain risk.
No evidence of clickjacking or iframe manipulation.

summary: The script interacts with api.torn.com using a user-provided API key stored in localStorage. No evidence of data exfiltration beyond the API key, no DOM XSS, no code obfuscation, and no supply chain risk. The main privacy concern is the handling of the API key. No sensitive browser APIs are used. Overall, the script is safe for its intended purpose, but users should be warned not to use private or sensitive API keys.
